title: The Spotlight Effect

scenes.narration: Nobody is watching you as closely as you think. And psychologists have a name for that feeling.
scenes.image_prompt: A young man standing alone under a single spotlight in a dark crowded room, everyone around him blurred and looking at their phones, tense expression
scenes.video_prompt: Slow push-in on the man's face as the spotlight flickers; blurred figures drift past in the background

scenes.narration: It's called the spotlight effect. We overestimate how much other people notice our looks, our mistakes, and our awkward moments.
scenes.image_prompt: A woman at a cafe table glancing nervously at a small coffee stain on her shirt, other customers absorbed in their own conversations, warm window light
scenes.video_prompt: Camera slowly orbits the woman as she looks down at the stain; customers keep chatting

scenes.narration: In one well-known study, students wore an embarrassing T-shirt into a room. They guessed about half the room noticed. In reality, far fewer did.
scenes.image_prompt: A college student entering a lecture hall wearing a loud, embarrassing graphic t-shirt, classmates mostly looking at laptops, overhead fluorescent light
scenes.video_prompt: Tracking shot following the student walking in; heads stay down on laptops

scenes.narration: Why does this happen? Because you are the center of your own world. You live inside your head all day, so you assume everyone else is looking at it too.
scenes.on_screen_text: You're the center of your world
scenes.image_prompt: Surreal image of a person standing in the middle of a city street while giant mirrors around them reflect only their own face, dusk lighting
scenes.video_prompt: Slow 360-degree rotation around the person as the mirrors shimmer

scenes.narration: But everyone else is busy doing the exact same thing. Worrying about themselves.
scenes.image_prompt: A busy subway car full of commuters each lost in their own thoughts, some anxious, some checking reflections, cinematic teal and orange grade
scenes.video_prompt: Slow lateral dolly along the subway car past each commuter's face

scenes.narration: So next time you trip, stumble over a word, or have a bad hair day, remember. Most people won't notice, and the ones who do will forget by tomorrow.
scenes.image_prompt: A confident woman laughing after tripping slightly on a city sidewalk, passersby continuing on their way, golden hour sunlight
scenes.video_prompt: Slow-motion shot of the woman regaining balance and smiling as people walk past

scenes.narration: Follow for more psychology that explains the way you think.
scenes.image_prompt: Glowing human brain made of light floating in a dark space with soft particles, mysterious and elegant
scenes.video_prompt: Brain slowly rotates while particles drift upward; gentle push-in

caption:
You're not as noticed as you think — and that's freeing. 🧠
What's an embarrassing moment you overthought for days?
